# Agent-runtime — local multi-agent compose
#
# Two long-running agent services plus RAG stack (qdrant, rag-server, indexer).
# The RAG stack is included by default — all services start with `docker compose up --build`.
# Agent-2 is commented out by default; uncomment to run two agents in parallel.
#
# restart: unless-stopped provides crash recovery only — the poll cadence is
# controlled by idle_sleep_seconds in agent.yaml (default: 60 s), not by
# container restarts.
#
# RAG stack (qdrant + rag-server + indexer) is enabled by default. Required:
#   1. Set RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH in .env to the path of your local rag-service clone.
#   2. Set WORKSPACE_ID in .env (e.g. "workspace").
#   3. Set WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH in .env to the path of your local workspace management
#      repo clone (e.g. "/path/to/project-workspace"). workspace.yaml is mounted read-only
#      into the indexer; the indexer resolves repos via SSH clone — no other mounts needed.
#
# Usage (from this directory):
#   cp agent.yaml.example agent.yaml   # fill in watches: with your workspace SSH URL
#   cp .env.example .env               # fill in required values (including RAG vars)
#   docker compose up --build          # start agents + RAG stack (default)
#   docker compose up --build -d       # start in background

name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-agent-runtime-local}

# ── Shared agent definition ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
x-agent: &agent-base
  build:
    # Build context is workflow/ root so schemas/ is included.
    # Path is three levels up: local/ → orchestration/ → agent-runtime/ → workflow/
    context: ../../..
    dockerfile: agent-runtime/Dockerfile
  env_file:
    - path: ${PROJECT_ENV_FILE:-.env}
      required: false
  environment:
    AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
    WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
    WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
    # Required for the pr-create skill (GitHub REST API).
    GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
    # SSH key delivery: SSH_PRIVATE_KEY (env var, preferred) or SSH_KEY_PATH (file mount).
    SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
    SSH_KEY_PATH: /agent/ssh/id_rsa
    # RAG context injection — enabled by default. Agents query the RAG server
    # for relevant project context before starting each task.
    # Defaults to the companion rag-server in this compose file.
    # Override in .env to point to an external RAG server, or set to empty to disable.
    MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"
  volumes:
    - ${AGENT_YAML_LOCAL_PATH:-./agent.yaml}:/agent/agent.yaml:ro
    - workspaces:/agent/data
    - workflow:/agent/workflow
    - ${SSH_KEY_DIR:-${HOME}/.ssh}:/agent/ssh:ro
  restart: unless-stopped
  deploy:
    resources:
      limits:
        cpus: "4"
        memory: 10G
      reservations:
        cpus: "1"
        memory: 2G

# ── Shared RAG build context ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both rag-server and indexer build from the rag-service repo.
# RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH must point to your local clone of the rag-service repo.
x-rag-build: &rag-build
  context: ${RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH:?Set RAG_SERVICE_LOCAL_PATH to the local path
    of your rag-service clone}
  dockerfile: Dockerfile

# ── Services ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
services:
  agent-1:
    <<: *agent-base
    environment:
      AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
      WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
      WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
      GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
      SSH_KEY_PATH: /agent/ssh/id_rsa
      GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "${GIT_AUTHOR_NAME}"
      GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "${GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL}"
      MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"

  # agent-2:
  #   <<: *agent-base
  #   environment:
  #     AGENT_YAML_PATH: /agent/agent.yaml
  #     WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH: /agent/workflow
  #     WORKSPACES_ROOT: /agent/data
  #     GITHUB_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
  #     SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
  #     SSH_KEY_PATH: /agent/ssh/id_rsa
  #     GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "Agent 2"
  #     GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "${GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL}"
  #     MCP_RAG_URL: "${MCP_RAG_URL:-http://rag-server:8000}"

  # ── digital-factory-ui ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Feature Status Dashboard v2 — local Next.js dev server.
  #
  # Required .env values:
  #   DIGITAL_FACTORY_UI_LOCAL_PATH — path to your local digital-factory-ui clone
  #   WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH — host directory containing workspace subdirectories (shared with agents)
  #   SSH_PRIVATE_KEY — SSH private key used for git push
  #   GIT_AUTHOR_NAME / GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL — identity for git commits written by the UI
  #
  # Usage:
  #   docker compose up digital-factory-ui --build
  #   Open http://localhost:5493
  digital-factory-ui:
    build:
      context: ${DIGITAL_FACTORY_UI_LOCAL_PATH:?Set DIGITAL_FACTORY_UI_LOCAL_PATH to your local digital-factory-ui clone path}
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    ports:
      - "${DIGITAL_FACTORY_UI_PORT:-5493}:3000"
    environment:
      WORKSPACE_LIST: /agent/data
      GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: "${GIT_AUTHOR_NAME}"
      GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: "${GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL}"
      SSH_PRIVATE_KEY: "${SSH_PRIVATE_KEY:-}"
    volumes:
      - ${WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH:?Set WORKSPACE_MGMT_LOCAL_PATH to the host directory for agent workspace data}:/agent/data:ro
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ── RAG stack (enabled by default) ───────────────────────────────────────────
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:latest
    ports:
      - "${QDRANT_PORT:-6333}:6333"
      - "${QDRANT_GRPC_PORT:-6334}:6334"
    volumes:
      - qdrant_data:/qdrant/storage
    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: "2"
          memory: 2G

# agent-runtime — fat multi-runtime image
#
# Runtimes included:
#   Node 20       agent-runtime TypeScript
#   Python 3.12   Airflow 3.1.3 compatibility
#   Go 1.25       Go services in operator stack
#
# Build context: workflow/ root (one level up from agent-runtime/)
#   docker build -f agent-runtime/Dockerfile .
#
# Build args:
#   GO_VERSION   default: 1.25.0  (override if 1.25 is not yet released: --build-arg GO_VERSION=1.24.2)
#   TARGETARCH   set automatically by docker buildx (amd64 | arm64)

# ── Stage 1: TypeScript builder ───────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /build

# Install dependencies first for better layer caching.
COPY agent-runtime/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

# Copy source and compile.
COPY agent-runtime/src/ ./src/
COPY agent-runtime/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

# Prune dev dependencies — only production modules go into the runtime image.
RUN npm prune --production

# ── Stage 2: Fat runtime image ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# python:3.12-slim-bookworm provides Python 3.12 out of the box.
# Node 20 and Go are layered on top.
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS runtime

ARG GO_VERSION=1.25.0
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64

# ── System packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        curl \
        ca-certificates \
        git \
        jq \
        openssh-client \
        tini \
        gnupg \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Node 20 via NodeSource ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Go ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN curl -fsSL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz" \
        -o /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && rm /tmp/go.tar.gz

ENV PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
ENV GOPATH="/go"
ENV PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"

# ── Package managers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# yarn is needed for repos that ship a yarn.lock (most implementation repos).
# pnpm is needed for repos that ship a pnpm-lock.yaml.
RUN npm install -g yarn pnpm

# ── Claude CLI ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Required by run-task.ts — spawned as a subprocess for each task activation.
# GITHUB_TOKEN must be injected at runtime (see DOCKER.md).
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# ── Workspace layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Mirror the local repo structure so relative schema paths resolve correctly.
# validate-agent-yaml.ts resolves: dist/config/../../.. → /workflow/schemas/
WORKDIR /workflow

# Schemas from the workflow root (needed by the AJV validators at runtime).
COPY schemas/ ./schemas/

# Agent-runtime app.
WORKDIR /workflow/agent-runtime

COPY --from=builder /build/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/package.json ./package.json

COPY agent-runtime/scripts/ ./scripts/
RUN chmod +x ./scripts/run-once.sh

# ── Non-root user ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Claude Code blocks --dangerously-skip-permissions when running as root.
# Run as a dedicated agent user so the flag is accepted.
#
# Named volume initialisation: Docker copies image directory contents (with
# their permissions) into a named volume on first use. Pre-creating /agent/*
# as agent-owned here ensures fresh volumes start writable by the agent user.
# If volumes already exist as root-owned, recreate them:
#   docker compose down -v && docker compose up --build
RUN useradd -m -u 1001 -s /bin/bash agent \
    && mkdir -p /agent/data /agent/ssh /agent/workflow /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chmod 700 /home/agent/.ssh \
    && chown -R agent:agent /agent /workflow /home/agent

# Relocate GOPATH so the module cache is writable by the agent user.
ENV GOPATH="/home/agent/go"
ENV PATH="/home/agent/go/bin:$PATH"

USER agent

# ── Foundry (forge, cast, anvil) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash \
    && /home/agent/.foundry/bin/foundryup
ENV PATH="/home/agent/.foundry/bin:$PATH"

# ── Container contract ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Required env vars — see DOCKER.md for full documentation.
ENV AGENT_YAML_PATH="/agent/agent.yaml"
ENV WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH="/agent/workflow"
ENV WORKSPACES_ROOT="/agent/data"

# Volume mounts (documented in DOCKER.md):
#   /agent/agent.yaml   — agent configuration (read-only)
#   /agent/data/        — workspace clones (read-write)
#   /agent/ssh/         — SSH key directory (read-only)

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "/workflow/agent-runtime/scripts/run-once.sh"]

/**
 * Briefing generator for the Claude executor.
 *
 * Produces a markdown briefing written to a temporary file before the executor
 * process is spawned. The briefing carries only task-specific context — it does
 * not contain workflow-protocol rules (those are the orchestrator's concern).
 *
 * Contrast with the old agent-runtime/src/bootstrap/agent-context.ts which also
 * injected /start-implementation and /pr-create invocations. After the
 * orchestrator/executor split those responsibilities move to orchestrator
 * side-effects; the briefing is task context only.
 */

export interface BriefingOpts {
  taskId: string;
  featureId: string;
  taskTitle: string;
  taskBranch: string;
  taskRepo: string;
  taskRepoRoot: string;
  workspaceRoot: string;
  gitAuthorEmail: string;
  gitAuthorName: string;
  implementationModel: string;
  resultPath: string;
}

/**
 * Generate the per-activation briefing markdown for the Claude executor.
 *
 * Sections (in order):
 *   1. Preamble — automated context, no interactive session
 *   2. ## Identity
 *   3. ## Your assigned task
 *   4. ## What you must do
 *   5. ## Model
 *   6. ## Rules
 */
export function generateBriefing(opts: BriefingOpts): string {
  const {
    taskId,
    featureId,
    taskTitle,
    taskBranch,
    taskRepo,
    taskRepoRoot,
    workspaceRoot,
    gitAuthorEmail,
    gitAuthorName,
    implementationModel,
    resultPath,
  } = opts;

  return [
    "You are an automated software agent running in a headless container.",
    "There is no interactive session. Do not prompt for input.",
    "Do not ask clarifying questions. Execute the task described below.",
    "",
    "## Identity",
    "",
    `Email: ${gitAuthorEmail}`,
    `Name:  ${gitAuthorName}`,
    "",
    "## Your assigned task",
    "",
    `Workspace root: ${workspaceRoot}`,
    `Feature:        ${featureId}`,
    `Task ID:        ${taskId}`,
    `Title:          ${taskTitle}`,
    `Impl repo:      ${taskRepo}`,
    `Repo root:      ${taskRepoRoot}`,
    `Branch:         ${taskBranch}`,
    "",
    "## What you must do",
    "",
    `1. Read the task specification from \`${workspaceRoot}/docs/features/${featureId}/tasks.md\``,
    `   under the heading \`## ${taskId} — ${taskTitle}\`.`,
    "2. Implement all required changes inside the implementation repo.",
    "   The repo has already been cloned and the branch is checked out.",
    "3. Run `/pr-self-review` on the completed branch.",
    "4. Run the test suite in two phases:",
    "   a. Unit tests first: `npm run test:unit` (or equivalent). Fix any failures.",
    "   b. Full suite once: `npm test`. Container resource timeouts on integration tests",
    "      that pass in isolation are not code bugs — confirm isolation pass and proceed.",
    "5. Commit and push all changes to the feature branch.",
    `6. Write a result file to \`${resultPath}\`:`,
    "   - On success (ready for review):",
    '     `{"terminal_status": "in_review"}`',
    "   - If blocked and cannot proceed:",
    '     `{"terminal_status": "blocked", "blocked_reason": "<reason>", "blocked_suggestion": "<next step>"}`',
    "",
    "Complete all steps without stopping or asking for confirmation.",
    "",
    "## Model",
    "",
    `Use model: ${implementationModel}`,
    "",
    "## Rules",
    "",
    "- Do not ask clarifying questions. Implement what is specified.",
    "- Do not open pull requests — the orchestrator handles PR creation after you exit.",
    "- Do not modify task YAML files or any management-repo workflow state.",
    `- You MUST write the result file to \`${resultPath}\` before exiting.`,
    "  If you are stuck and cannot write it, the orchestrator will mark the task blocked.",
    "- If a shell command exits with code 127 (command not found), immediately write",
    '  `{"terminal_status": "blocked", "blocked_reason": "missing_tool"}` and exit.',
    "  Do not attempt workarounds — this is a container image problem.",
  ].join("\n");
}

# orchestrator — lean image
#
# Contains only Node + git; no language toolchains.
# The Claude executor binary is baked into the same image on day 1
# (single-container deployment per D1).
#
# Build context: workflow/ root
#   docker build -f runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile .

# ── Stage 1: TypeScript builder ───────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS builder

WORKDIR /build/abi
COPY runtime/abi/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY runtime/abi/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/abi/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

WORKDIR /build/orchestrator
COPY runtime/orchestrator/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci

COPY runtime/orchestrator/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/orchestrator/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

# ── Stage 2: executor builder ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-bookworm-slim AS executor-builder

WORKDIR /build/abi
COPY runtime/abi/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/abi/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/abi/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build

WORKDIR /build/executor
COPY runtime/executors/claude/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY runtime/executors/claude/src/ ./src/
COPY runtime/executors/claude/tsconfig.json ./
RUN npm run build
RUN npm prune --production

# ── Stage 3: Runtime image ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS runtime

ARG GO_VERSION=1.25.0
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        curl \
        ca-certificates \
        git \
        jq \
        openssh-client \
        tini \
        gnupg \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Node 20 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ── Go ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN curl -fsSL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-${TARGETARCH}.tar.gz" \
        -o /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && tar -C /usr/local -xzf /tmp/go.tar.gz \
    && rm /tmp/go.tar.gz

ENV PATH="/usr/local/go/bin:$PATH"
ENV GOPATH="/go"
ENV PATH="$GOPATH/bin:$PATH"

# ── Package managers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN npm install -g yarn pnpm

# ── Claude CLI ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# ── Workspace layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
WORKDIR /workflow

COPY schemas/ ./schemas/

# Orchestrator
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/orchestrator
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/orchestrator/package.json ./package.json

# ABI (shared)
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/abi
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=builder /build/abi/package.json ./package.json

# Claude executor (baked in for day-1 single-container deployment)
WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/executors/claude
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/executor/dist ./dist/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/executor/node_modules ./node_modules/
COPY --from=executor-builder /build/executor/package.json ./package.json

# ── Non-root user ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
RUN useradd -m -u 1001 -s /bin/bash agent \
    && mkdir -p /agent/data /agent/ssh /agent/workflow /home/agent/.ssh \

ENV GOPATH="/home/agent/go"
ENV PATH="/home/agent/go/bin:$PATH"

USER agent

RUN curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash \

ENV PATH="/home/agent/.foundry/bin:$PATH"

ENV AGENT_YAML_PATH="/agent/agent.yaml"
ENV WORKFLOW_LOCAL_PATH="/agent/workflow"
ENV WORKSPACES_ROOT="/agent/data"

WORKDIR /workflow/runtime/orchestrator

ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--", "node", "dist/main.js"]

content.content:
## T2 — Big-bang split — extract orchestrator + Claude executor, cutover

### Description

The cutover PR. Per technical-design §4 and §6, T2 is one PR that:

- Creates `workflow/runtime/orchestrator/` and moves the polling loop,
  claim, poll, eligibility, bootstrap, and briefing-generation code
  into it. Most of the diff is git-detected file renames + import-path
  updates.
- Creates `workflow/runtime/executors/claude/` and moves the body of
  `agent-runtime/src/loop/run-claude.ts` into it as the ABI-conformant
  entrypoint: reads env vars per `ExecutorInput`, runs `claude -p`,
  writes `result.json` per `ExecutorResult`, exits 0/non-zero.
- Implements `SubProcessAdapter` (TD-A2) in
  `runtime/orchestrator/src/adapter/spawn.ts`: spawns the Claude
  executor binary as a child process inside the same container,
  serializes `ExecutorInput` into env vars, waits for exit, reads and
  validates `result.json`.
- **Moves workflow side effects** from inside-Claude responsibility to
  orchestrator code (`runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/`):
  PR open, task YAML mutation (`in_progress → in_review/blocked`),
  dependency unblock (auto-ready rule), log entries, branch sync.
  Today these are partly performed by Claude via `pr-create` skill +
  CLAUDE.md guidance; after T2 they are deterministic orchestrator
  code triggered by reading `result.json`.
- Updates the briefing-generation logic so the briefing markdown
  carries task-specific context only — workflow rules stop being
  injected into Claude's runtime context.
- Replaces the single bundled Dockerfile with two Dockerfiles:
  `runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile` (lean — Node + git + GH token) and
  `runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile` (Node + Claude CLI + task
  toolchains). On day 1 the deployed image can still bake both
  binaries together; the choice is per-deployment.
- Updates `docker-compose` template to point at new images.
- **Deletes** `workflow/agent-runtime/` entirely, including K8s
  CronJob and GH Actions templates (they would otherwise orphan
  pointing at removed paths — re-introduction is a follow-on
  feature).

T2 includes a final subtask: walk the migrated `runtime/orchestrator/`
package with fresh eyes and populate the concrete refactor checklist
under T5's `### Subtasks` section. T5's scope cannot be enumerated
until the split lands; T2's last act is to enumerate it.

T2 does **not** include orchestrator-internal refactors — those defer
to T5. T2 also does not include test rewrites — those defer to T3
(though existing tests must be migrated to the new layout and
continue to pass).

End-to-end smoke gate: before merging T2's PR, drive one real task
through the new shape on a non-production workspace and verify
claim → PR open → merge handoff.

### Required skills

- typescript-best-practices

### Subtasks

- [ ] Create `workflow/runtime/orchestrator/` package skeleton (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `Dockerfile`)
- [ ] Create `workflow/runtime/executors/claude/` package skeleton (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `Dockerfile`)
- [ ] Move polling loop, claim, poll, eligibility, bootstrap from `agent-runtime/src/` to `runtime/orchestrator/src/` with import paths updated
- [ ] Move `agent-runtime/src/bootstrap/agent-context.ts` to `runtime/orchestrator/src/briefing/` and rename to reflect briefing semantics
- [ ] Move `agent-runtime/src/loop/run-claude.ts` body into `runtime/executors/claude/src/index.ts` as the ABI-conformant entrypoint
- [ ] Implement `SubProcessAdapter` in `runtime/orchestrator/src/adapter/spawn.ts`: env-var serialization, child spawn, wait, validate result.json
- [ ] Wire `runtime/orchestrator/src/main.ts` to instantiate `SubProcessAdapter` and call it from the dispatch step
- [ ] Move PR open from `pr-create` skill invocation to `runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/open-pr.ts` (orchestrator-side)
- [ ] Move task YAML mutation (in_progress → in_review/blocked) from inside-Claude flow to `runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/mutate-task-yaml.ts`
- [ ] Move dependency unblock (auto-ready rule) to `runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/unblock-deps.ts`
- [ ] Move log-entry appending to `runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/append-log.ts`
- [ ] Update briefing template: remove runtime-injected workflow rules; carry task description, quality bar, model policy, RAG context only
- [ ] Migrate existing tests to compile against new package layout (no logic changes — that is T3's scope)
- [ ] Update `docker-compose` template to reference the new orchestrator image (and bundled Claude binary on day 1)
- [ ] Delete `workflow/agent-runtime/` directory entirely (source, Dockerfile, all `templates/*` including K8s CronJob and GH Actions)
- [ ] End-to-end smoke gate: drive one real task through the new shape on a non-production workspace; verify claim → PR open → merge handoff before merging this PR
- [ ] **(Final)** Walk migrated `runtime/orchestrator/` with fresh eyes; populate concrete refactor checklist under T5's `### Subtasks` section in `tasks.md`

---

## T3 — Test migration + seam tests against fake executor

### Description

After T2 lands, the new package layout exists but is exercised only by
the migrated unit tests carried over from `agent-runtime/`. T3 adds
the test coverage that the split was meant to enable: orchestrator-
side end-to-end against `FakeAdapter`, exercising the ABI seam without
ever invoking Claude.

Three test layers:

1. **Orchestrator side-effects unit tests** — exercise `open-pr.ts`,
   `mutate-task-yaml.ts`, `unblock-deps.ts`, `append-log.ts` in
   isolation. Use in-memory fakes for the management-repo file system
   and a recorded GitHub API response for PR open.

2. **Seam tests against `FakeAdapter`** — drive
   `runtime/orchestrator/src/main.ts` (or a test entrypoint that uses
   the same dispatch) with `FakeAdapter` injected. Cover:
   - `in_review` happy path → orchestrator opens PR, mutates YAML,
     appends log, applies dep unblock if applicable
   - `blocked` with reason + suggestion → orchestrator marks blocked,
     records reason/suggestion
   - `failed` (executor non-zero exit, no result.json) → orchestrator
     marks blocked with `executor_crashed`
   - schema-invalid `result.json` → orchestrator marks failed with
     `result_schema_invalid`
   - wall-clock timeout → orchestrator kills child, marks blocked
     with `executor_timeout`

3. **Claude executor smoke test** — drive
   `runtime/executors/claude/src/index.ts` directly with a fixture
   briefing and assert the `result.json` shape and exit code. Does
   not invoke a real LLM; uses Claude CLI's dry-run / fixture mode if
   available, or a stub `claude` binary on `PATH` for the test.

T3 runs in parallel with T4 and T5 after T2 lands.

### Required skills

- typescript-best-practices

### Subtasks

- [ ] Add unit tests for `open-pr.ts` against in-memory + recorded GitHub fixtures
- [ ] Add unit tests for `mutate-task-yaml.ts` covering all terminal_status cases
- [ ] Add unit tests for `unblock-deps.ts` covering: no unblock, single unblock, multiple unblocks, partial dep satisfaction
- [ ] Add unit tests for `append-log.ts` covering action enum + timestamp + actor fields
- [ ] Add seam test: in_review happy path with `FakeAdapter`
- [ ] Add seam test: blocked with reason + suggestion
- [ ] Add seam test: executor non-zero exit (no result.json) → `executor_crashed`
- [ ] Add seam test: schema-invalid result.json → `result_schema_invalid`
- [ ] Add seam test: wall-clock timeout → `executor_timeout`
- [ ] Add Claude executor smoke test driving the entrypoint with a fixture briefing
- [ ] Verify all tests pass on the new package layout

---

## T4 — Documentation update — flesh out abi-spec.md, split CLAUDE.md, handoff

### Description

Documentation closes out the cutover for human readers and future
runtime authors.

Four documents land in this task:

1. **`runtime/abi/docs/abi-spec.md`** — flesh out the skeleton from
   T1. The spec doc is the authoritative contract a third-party
   runtime author pins against. Document: ABI input env vars and

/**
 * Briefing generator for the Claude executor.
 *
 * Produces a markdown briefing written to a temporary file before the executor
 * process is spawned. The briefing carries only task-specific context — it does
 * not contain workflow-protocol rules (those are the orchestrator's concern).
 *
 * Contrast with the old agent-runtime/src/bootstrap/agent-context.ts which also
 * injected /start-implementation and /pr-create invocations. After the
 * orchestrator/executor split those responsibilities move to orchestrator
 * side-effects; the briefing is task context only.
 */

export interface BriefingOpts {
  taskId: string;
  featureId: string;
  taskTitle: string;
  taskBranch: string;
  taskRepo: string;
  taskRepoRoot: string;
  workspaceRoot: string;
  gitAuthorEmail: string;
  gitAuthorName: string;
  implementationModel: string;
  resultPath: string;
}

/**
 * Generate the per-activation briefing markdown for the Claude executor.
 *
 * Sections (in order):
 *   1. Preamble — automated context, no interactive session
 *   2. ## Identity
 *   3. ## Your assigned task
 *   4. ## What you must do
 *   5. ## Model
 *   6. ## Rules
 */
export function generateBriefing(opts: BriefingOpts): string {
  const {
    taskId,
    featureId,
    taskTitle,
    taskBranch,
    taskRepo,
    taskRepoRoot,
    workspaceRoot,
    gitAuthorEmail,
    gitAuthorName,
    implementationModel,
    resultPath,
  } = opts;

  return [
    "You are an automated software agent running in a headless container.",
    "There is no interactive session. Do not prompt for input.",
    "Do not ask clarifying questions. Execute the task described below.",
    "",
    "## Identity",
    "",
    `Email: ${gitAuthorEmail}`,
    `Name:  ${gitAuthorName}`,
    "",
    "## Your assigned task",
    "",
    `Workspace root: ${workspaceRoot}`,
    `Feature:        ${featureId}`,
    `Task ID:        ${taskId}`,
    `Title:          ${taskTitle}`,
    `Impl repo:      ${taskRepo}`,
    `Repo root:      ${taskRepoRoot}`,
    `Branch:         ${taskBranch}`,
    "",
    "## What you must do",
    "",
    `1. Read the task specification from \`${workspaceRoot}/docs/features/${featureId}/tasks.md\``,
    `   under the heading \`## ${taskId} — ${taskTitle}\`.`,
    "2. Implement all required changes inside the implementation repo.",
    "   The repo has already been cloned and the branch is checked out.",
    "3. Run `/pr-self-review` on the completed branch.",
    "4. Run the test suite in two phases:",
    "   a. Unit tests first: `npm run test:unit` (or equivalent). Fix any failures.",
    "   b. Full suite once: `npm test`. Container resource timeouts on integration tests",
    "      that pass in isolation are not code bugs — confirm isolation pass and proceed.",
    "5. Commit and push all changes to the feature branch.",
    `6. Write a result file to \`${resultPath}\`:`,
    "   - On success (ready for review):",
    '     `{"terminal_status": "in_review"}`',
    "   - If blocked and cannot proceed:",
    '     `{"terminal_status": "blocked", "blocked_reason": "<reason>", "blocked_suggestion": "<next step>"}`',
    "",
    "Complete all steps without stopping or asking for confirmation.",
    "",
    "## Model",
    "",
    `Use model: ${implementationModel}`,
    "",
    "## Rules",
    "",
    "- Do not ask clarifying questions. Implement what is specified.",
    "- Do not open pull requests — the orchestrator handles PR creation after you exit.",
    "- Do not modify task YAML files or any management-repo workflow state.",
    `- You MUST write the result file to \`${resultPath}\` before exiting.`,
    "  If you are stuck and cannot write it, the orchestrator will mark the task blocked.",
    "- If a shell command exits with code 127 (command not found), immediately write",
    '  `{"terminal_status": "blocked", "blocked_reason": "missing_tool"}` and exit.',
    "  Do not attempt workarounds — this is a container image problem.",
  ].join("\n");
}
